data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli army suicides reach highest level since 2010: Press review
data.author: Hossam Desouky
data.summary:
Israeli army suicides reach highest level since 2010: Press review
Israeli military suicides reach 16-year high
A total of 23 serving Israeli military personnel have died by suicide since the beginning of this year, the highest number recorded in the army since 2010, Haaretz reported on Monday.
At least 17 former soldiers also died by suicide in the past year, shortly after being discharged from military service, bringing the total number of serving and former soldiers who took their own lives to 40.
Suicides are not confined to Israel's military. Haaretz noted that five police officers also died by suicide in 2026.
According to official Israeli military data cited by the report, 73 officers and soldiers have died by suicide since the Hamas-led attacks in southern Israel on 7 October.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli contestant with 'peace' costume booed at Miss Universe 2026
data.author: Hannah. Smith
data.summary:
Israeli contestant with 'peace' costume booed at Miss Universe 2026
Submitted by
Hannah. Smith
on
Mon, 11/23/2026 - 14:12
Social media users slam 'audacity' of dress amid Israel’s genocide in Gaza and wars in the region
Miss Israel 2026 Danielle Yablonka, who describes herself as a Zionist, on stage during the national costume segment of the Miss Universe competition (Screengrab/Instagram: @missisrael)
Off
Miss Israel was booed on stage during the national costume portion of the Miss Universe pageant in Puerto Rico this weekend.
As Danielle Yablonka stepped out in a gold jewelled bodice, boots and crown, she spread her arms to reveal a cape depicting olive trees and Jaffa oranges, with the word “peace” written in English, Hebrew and Arabic running along the bottom.
After she came to a stop and posed for the judges, she was immediately met with loud boos that even the music couldn’t cover.
Turning around to reveal the back of the garment, she kept her arms held out to show the audience the warm-toned depiction of East Jerusalem, featuring the vibrant gold and blue of Al-Aqsa Mosque complex in the centre, surrounded by the Old City.
East Jerusalem is considered occupied under international law. It is also envisioned as the capital of an independent Palestinian state - not a part of Israel.
The glossy image - not a real photo - did not reflect the ongoing demolition of Palestinian homes in the city, and featured the word Jerusalem in English, Hebrew and Arabic.
The costume choice for the 25-year-old Miami-born model was met with fierce criticism on social media, with users pointing out the ongoing ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and the genocide in Gaza.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US could send troops back to Syria in training role, says report
data.author: MEE staff

US could send troops back to Syria in training role, says report
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Mon, 11/23/2026 - 20:02
Demining operation could be expanded and comes as Saudi Arabia looks to Syrian military advisers for help against Houthis
Syrian government troops near the city of Hasakeh on 2 February 2026 (Bakr Alkasem/AFP)
Off
The US is weighing a plan to train Syrian soldiers in demining in what would be the first US military training mission in Syria since President Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power.
Reuters reported on Monday that the training operation is still under discussion, but if it is agreed it will mark a return of US troops to Syria after they have just completed a withdrawal.
The last remaining US troops left their last base in Hasakah, Syria, in April, ending a 10-year presence in the country.
The US kept thousands of soldiers in Syria as part of operations to defeat the Islamic State (IS) group. At least 2,000 US troops remained in the country ostensibly to defeat IS but also to counter Iran.
In 2024, Ahmed al-Sharaa led a military offensive that ousted Bashar al-Assad, an Iranian ally, from power.
The programme would be part of the Damascus Coordination Center, set up last year in Jordan to facilitate cooperation between Syrian authorities, the US and its regional allies. Reuters said that cooperation could be expanded beyond demining.
The return of US troops would come at a time when Saudi Arabia, a key US ally, is looking to Syrian military advisers to help fight the Houthis in Yemen. A western official previously told MEE that some Syrian drone specialists had already arrived in Yemen to assist the Saudi-backed forces.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Benghazi drone attack: Is Ukraine opening a Mediterranean front against Russia?
data.author: Omar Ashour
data.summary:
Benghazi drone attack: Is Ukraine opening a Mediterranean front against Russia?
Submitted by
Omar Ashour
on
Mon, 11/23/2026 - 11:54
The strategic test is whether repeated attacks constrain Moscow’s ability to sustain its war and overseas military deployments
A satellite image shows smoke rising from a burning ship in the Libyan port of Benghazi. Ukraine claimed it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya on 23 November, 2026 (AFP)
Off
On Monday, hours after Ukraine claimed responsibility for the drone attack that sank Russian warship at Libyan naval base, Ukraine Security Service (SBU) said in a statement that "Russia’s military fleet and its logistics networks have no safe routes even far beyond the Black Sea."
The wreckage at Benghazi gave that warning substance.
Kyiv says seven Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury, destroyed its Ka-27 helicopter and also struck the weapons transport ship MV Angara.
Satellite imagery showed the corvette capsized. Commissioned in 2023, Merkury was a modern combatant, designed to fight ships and submarines and defend against air attack. Ukraine - a country deprived of most of its conventional navy as of 2014 following Russia's annexation of Crimea - is extending maritime attrition into Russia’s Mediterranean foothold in 2026.
As previously argued in Middle East Eye, maritime denial can defeat a superior navy’s strategic objectives without winning conventional fleet battles.
Benghazi is the latest proof.
A campaign across seas
The 11 named vessels in Ukrainian-claimed or suspected incidents since August 2025 illustrate four overlapping target sets. The first is "sea combatants", exemplified by Merkury.
The second is "military transport": Angara was struck near Benghazi while Sparta II was hit in the Gulf of Finland while bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio with Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani in Washington, 23 November 2026 (Kylie Cooper/Reuters)
Off
Qatar's prime minister said on Monday that the region will not be able to tolerate another outbreak of attacks between the US and Iran, and that his country is pushing to revive stalled peace talks.
Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani made the comments to Al Jazeera after meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington.
"The situation in the Middle East cannot afford a new escalation between the US and Iran," he said.
He added that Doha and Washington are also seeking to boost their military engagement.
Qatar is home to the largest US military base in the Middle East, and hosts the regional headquarters of US Central Command.
"Strategic dialogue with the US is central to our relationship, and we aim to strengthen cooperation in defence," Thani told Al Jazeera.
Qatar was repeatedly targeted by Iran during the height of the US-Israeli war on Iran, suffering major damage to infrastructure that curtailed its ability to produce the energy that drives its economy. The continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is compounding the strain on its economic engine.
This comes as Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said on Monday that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stressed that the "no war, no peace situation cannot continue and should be resolved", according to the Tasnim news agency.
"The enemy wants to impose a no-war, no-peace situation to drain us," Ghalibaf said. "The question now is how, by whom, and with what actions should we resolve this situation."
